title: Vault emergency procedures and credential ledger
content:
Purpose
This runbook captures emergency (break-glass) procedures, credential inventory ledger conventions, rotation automation guidance, and audit/SIEM export mappings for Redwood Inference secrets management. It supplements technical runbooks (vault ops, KMS integrations) with cross-team escalation steps and evidence-capture requirements for compliance reviews.

Scope
- HashiCorp Vault primary namespace (hosted and dedicated clusters)
- Customer-facing escrow keys in sealed HSMs / AWS KMS / GCP KMS
- Break-glass artifacts (emergency tokens, one-off SSH keys)
- Rotation jobs and audit exports to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog)
- RBAC v2 role mappings that grant Just-in-Time (JIT) access

High-level principles
1) Minimal standing privileges: use RBAC v2 role templates; prefer ephemeral tokens and leased credentials.
2) Observable emergency actions: every break-glass activation must create tamper-evident evidence (ticket, signed acknowledgement, captured stdout, recorded session).
3) Automation-first rotations: schedule and verify rotations with automated smoke tests; keep rollback plans.
4) Immutable audit schema: do not change required audit fields without security review.

Quick contacts (oncall & escalation)
- Vault oncall: eng-sre rotation pager (pager duty)
- Security lead (incident): Maya Chen (owner)
- Compliance lead: Priya Nair
- Legal: Diego Alvarez
- Slack channel: #sec-ops-emergency

Break-glass activation flow (emergency read / recovery)
Preconditions:
- Confirm that normal vault unseal/unlock and SRE procedures have been attempted per standard vault incident doc.
- Manager approval required unless a system-wide outage; if not reachable, two SRE oncall acknowledgements suffice.
Steps: 
1) Open a Jira ticket with label security:break-glass and populate: summary, justification, affected systems, start_time (ISO8601), approver names. Attach any monitoring evidence.
2) Post a concise activation notice in #sec-ops-emergency including the Jira ticket link.
3) Generate an emergency token using the constrained emergency policy (duration = 1 hour, max-uses = 1, scope = read-only / targeted path) from the vault emergency namespace. Example: vault token create -policy=\"emergency-read-only\" -orphan -ttl=1h 
4) Record token metadata to the credential ledger (see ledger conventions below). Persist only the token ID (hashed) and ticket ref — do NOT store the raw token in a plaintext document. Store encrypted artifact in the escrow bucket (SSE-KMS).
5) All actions performed under that token must be logged and associated to the Jira ticket. Operators must record command history and copy terminal output to the ticket. If accessing via SSH, start a session recording (ttyrec) and upload to the evidence bucket.
6) After operation, token must be immediately revoked: vault token revoke <token-id>. Attach revocation evidence (revocation API response) to the Jira ticket.
7) Post incident summary in #sec-ops-emergency and to the compliance inbox.

Credential ledger conventions (what to capture)
- ledger_id: auto-generated short id (e.g., CL-2024-078)
- item_name: human-friendly short name (e.g., prod/db-master-rota-key)
- storage_type: vault/kms/hsm/ssh
- owner: team name / oncall at time of creation
- allowed_roles: RBAC v2 role ids (comma separated)
- last_rotation: ISO8601 timestamp
- rotation_cadence: e.g., 90d, 7d for short-lived secrets
- escrow_location: s3://sec-escrow/prod/… (only pointer)
- evidence_ticket: JIRA-####
- audit_reference: audit_event_id or splunk search id

Storage note: ledger rows stored in secure admin DB (encrypted at rest) and exported to compliance-only read views. Exports redact secret material and show only pointers and metadata.

Rotation automation patterns
- Use job-runner (Airflow / Nomad) to run rotation playbooks. Each rotation job must:
  * create new credential in target system via API
  * update dependent config (k8s secret, env store) in a transactional manner (canary -> full rollout)
  * run canary smoke test (connect + lightweight auth exercise)
  * on success, mark previous credential as revoked and record in ledger
  * on failure, roll back to previous credential and open incident
- Scheduling: production DB creds default 30d rotation for non-session keys; service-to-service long-lived keys use asymmetric key rotation with 1yr rotation but maintain short-lived session tokens.
- Secrets that are customer-managed (private deployments) are rotated on the customer's schedule; Redwood provides automation hooks and signed evidence for audits.

RBAC v2 specifics relevant to secrets
- Role templates: reader, operator, admin, emergency-operator (limited scope).
- Bindings must include justification and ticket ID for emergency roles.
- For JIT access, use OIDC-backed session tokens tied to an approval flow. Approval records are logged in the audit stream with approver and TTL.

Audit log schema (required fields)
Required fields (immutable):
- event_id: unique id (uuid v4)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- actor_id: user/email/service account
- actor_role: RBAC v2 role applied at time of action
- action: canonical verb (read/write/create/revoke/unseal/rotate/approve)
- resource_type: vault-secret/kms-key/ssh-key/hsm-key
- resource_id: path or key identifier
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- request_id: tracing id propagated from the request
- ticket_ref: optional Jira ticket id when associated
- evidence_refs: comma-separated pointers to session recordings / artifacts
Optional helpful fields:
- client_ip, region, agent_string, kv_version, lease_id, ttl_seconds

SIEM export mappings & parsers (Splunk example)
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON with the audit schema above.
- Splunk ingestion: index=security_audit sourcetype=vault_audit ndjson
- Recommended parsers: extract event_id, actor_id, action, resource_type, ticket_ref. Sample search: 
  index=security_audit sourcetype=vault_audit action=rotate | stats count by resource_type, outcome
- Alert rules to implement: 
  * Break-glass token creation alert: action=create AND actor_role=emergency-operator AND ttl_seconds>=3600 -> page sec-oncall
  * Excessive failed reads: action=read outcome=failure earliest=-15m | stats count by actor_id | where count>50 -> open ticket
  * Unscheduled rotation: action=rotate AND ticket_ref=\"\" -> auto-enqueue SOX review
- Evidence export cadence: daily roll-up of rotation events, immediate export of break-glass events to the compliance bucket (immutable storage).

Evidence automation (collection and retention)
- When emergency or rotation actions occur, trigger evidence capture lambda to:
  * snapshot the last 1h of relevant audit events (by request_id)
  * copy session recordings to immutable evidence store (WORM S3 with KMS key)
  * generate a signed metadata envelope (sha256) and attach to Jira ticket
- Retention: default 7y for break-glass and rotation evidence for regulated customers; 1y for routine rotation logs. Retention is configurable per customer plan.

Post-incident review checklist
- Verify ledger entries updated (pre/post rotation).
- Validate that all emergency tokens were revoked and revocation evidence attached.
- Check for any rekey or HSM changes and confirm backups were created and stored in escrow.
- Run SIEM queries to surface any lateral activity during the incident window. Save query results to ticket.
- Draft incident summary with timestamped timeline, root cause hypothesis, and remediation actions.

Operational playbook snippets (commands & examples)
- Create constrained emergency token:
  vault token create -policy=\"emergency-read-only\" -orphan -ttl=1h -display-name=\"eg-token-<JIRA-###>\"
- Revoke token:
  vault token revoke <token-id>
- Rotate KMS key (AWS - high level):
  * Create new key version / re-import key material in HSM
  * Update alias to point to new key ARN (rotate aliases vault plugin)
  * Rewrap stored ciphertext via vault rewrap utility
- Capture audit for request id:
  curl -s \"https://vault.internal/api/audit/events?request_id=<id>\" | jq . > evidence/<ledger_id>/request_<id>.json

Privacy & access considerations
- Do not include PII in ledger notes. Use user ids and ticket references.
- Evidence store access limited to secops, compliance, legal. Requests from other teams must go through documented process and be timeboxed.

Open items / TODOs
- Define RBAC v2 role-to-privilege mapping doc (in progress, assigned to Liam)
- Add automated approval hooks to Jira for emergency flow (design doc due Q1 2025)
- Produce signed audit-schema versioning policy (owner: Priya)

Appendix: sample event (ndjson line)
{"event_id":"b6f7e9a2-6b8f-4c3a-9d3e-3f2c8a1b2d9a","timestamp":"2024-11-30T14:22:08Z","actor_id":"alice@redwood.com","actor_role":"emergency-operator","action":"create","resource_type":"vault-secret","resource_id":"secret/data/prod/db/password","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-7c3f2a","ticket_ref":"JIRA-SECU-4123","evidence_refs":"s3://evidence/CL-2024-078/ttyrec-20241130-1422.rec"}

Notes on uniqueness
This document emphasizes ledger conventions and evidence automation wiring (signed envelopes, WORM storage, request_id snapshotting) and ties the break-glass flow directly to ticketing and SIEM exports. It intentionally focuses on minimizing standing privileges via RBAC v2 and JIT while presenting concrete automation patterns for rotation and evidence capture.

Owner contact: maya.chen@redwood.com
